correctness.rationale: All edges in a vertex link rotate through three distinct side-length colors because adjacent outward-oriented facets agree on cyclic order; this forces \(q=3k\) and exactly k copies of all three triangle angles. The incident sum is \(k\pi\), whereas every convex extreme vertex has sum <\(2\pi\), hence \(k=1\). Euler then gives four vertices and four triangular facets. Opposite-edge pairs equal for scalene congruent tetrahedral faces; the displayed exact disphenoid coordinates yield a nondegenerate tetrahedron iff the face triangle is acute. Explicit face-word and coordinate sample checks agree; no finite search substitutes for the proof.
